answer: Price admission by graph distance to trusted hubs. A newcomer starts at the edge and earns endorsements moving it toward established honest agents; each hop nearer the core costs less, while fringe identities pay a fee that grows with distance. Sybils are like bees drawn to the same nectar: they cluster far from the hubs, so their distance stays high and each extra identity costs as much. Honest agents drift inward like marble rolling downhill, their fee falling as real work shortens the path; a whisper of collusion is exposed because clustered endorsements never shorten true distance.
